Forecast Discussion

High pressure gives us mild and dry weather through Wednesday.

On Thursday, low pressure moves through the Ohio Valley and swings a strong cold front through western NC. The air behind the front is much colder. Upper level energy moves through Thursday night and Friday developing a low off the mid-Atlantic coast.

The combination of the instability (cold air over warm), upper level energy, cyclonic flow around the low bringing moisture and lift provided by the mountains will produce rain showers early Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon. Rain showers will turn to snow showers late Thursday night (beginning in the higher elevations and from west to east) and continue until Friday night/early Saturday morning. It will be much colder with strong and gusty winds as well so truly a shock to the system after such a mild and pleasant stretch we are having.

Saturday remains cold windy and cloudy but the snow shower action winds down. High pressure builds in Sunday and into early next week. Winds relax, skies clear and temperatures gradually warm under the high pressure.

Here is a preview of the snow totals we expect. Higher elevations have a greater potential for significant snow accumulations. The valleys and lower elevations likely get a period of snow showers Friday but surface temperatures will be above freezing so not much in the way of accumulations until after the sun goes down Friday evening. Accumulations in the valleys should be light compared to the ridge tops.
